papers.title: Bridging the QC–QA Cognitive Handoff: An Agentic Verification Harness for Error Detection, Specification Cross-Checking and Quality Documentation Assembly in Pharmaceutical Quality Assurance
papers.summary: Abstract Background. Quality control (QC) results reach regulatory dossiers through manual transcription and review. Such a benchmark does not yet exist. No collection of pharmaceutical quality documents carries discrepancies of known class and location, so automated verification cannot yet be evaluated against measured performance across realistic transfer errors and document types. Objectives. To specify (i) an architecture in which large language models only read and propose values, deterministic code performs every calculation and acceptance test, and a qualified reviewer makes every decision; (ii) a protocol for building a reference corpus and evaluating such systems; and (iii) sensitivity estimates from three dossiers. The plan covers design, evaluation, and measurement. Methods. Records from three ASEAN Common Technical Dossier Part II submissions (13, 14 and 10 records) were de-identified, and 112, 100 and 120 discrepancies across nine classes were introduced into dossiers A, B and C. A finding counted as a detection when it identified an injected discrepancy at the correct location with the correct class. The framework ran blind to the register. Sensitivity to injected discrepancies is reported per dossier with Wilson 95% confidence intervals and pooled by random-effects meta-analysis; clustering within records is not accounted for. Results. papers.title: An Auditable Multi-Agent Forum for Scientific Workflows with a Computational MOF Case Study
papers.summary: Scientific research increasingly combines large language models, computational tools and automated laboratories, creating a need to link hypotheses, assumptions, artifacts and revisions. We present Core-Forum, a persistent multi-agent forum architecture designed to organize these records in a common research thread. Its agent-package specification separates role kernels, model bindings, knowledge sources, tool permissions, artifact schemas and validation obligations. Retained interfaces illustrate role organization and protocol/artifact handoff; they do not establish a sample-linked MOF laboratory experiment or a controlled evaluation of the architecture. The quantitative case study instead reuses database-derived MOF pore descriptors and gas-uptake records. A corrected bounded geometric closure defines the dimensionless coordinate D W , while a fixed-radius unit-cell index D L supplies a comparative structural summary. Across 155,600 name-deduplicated admissible records, the fixed-radius association has R² = 0.4967. Sensitivity scenarios and within-gas holdout baselines delimit descriptor utility. D W is a deterministic nonlinear transformation of its geometric inputs, not a universal adsorption predictor. This study presents a workflow design and reproducible computational case; experimental closed-loop discovery and multi-agent performance gains remain to be evaluated.

papers.title: When, Where, and How Experience Becomes Structure: Mechanisms for Recursive Self-Improvement in LLM Agents
papers.summary: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) studies how AI systems modify themselves and carry those changes into the generation of subsequent improvements. LLM agents can pursue this process by using interaction experience to revise Prompt, Memory, Skill, and Harness in some cases while keeping the task-execution model’s weights fixed. However, execution feedback does not directly specify which component should change, and a locally successful revision may not remain useful across tasks or subsequent improvement cycles. Understanding how experience becomes persistent agent structure therefore requires examining when evidence justifies a change, where that change should act, and how it is constructed, verified, and retained. This survey connects four components--Prompt, Memory, Skill, and Harness--with seven analytical functions: Collect, Evaluate, Diagnose, Abstract, Update, Verify, and Consolidate. The resulting framework supports comparisons of instruction revision, memory management, skill construction and maintenance, and Harness evolution through their update loops. These comparisons examine how mechanisms use observations to construct candidate changes, distinguishing feedback that triggers revision from evidence that supports retention. The analysis further addresses coordinated updates across components and the revision or retirement of retained components as tasks, tools, and mo

papers.title: Self-directed coaching: repositioning the client as the internalizing agent of developmental self-regulation a conceptual framework and research agenda for coaching theory and practice
papers.summary: Coaching has become one of the most widely deployed developmental interventions in organizational, educational, and health-professions settings, and the literature offers substantial evidence for its short-term benefits. Evidence on whether those benefits persist after formal coaching support is withdrawn is thinner and less systematic, and the question points to an unresolved tension at the field’s core. Coaching is justified by its capacity to build independent, self-regulating professionals, but it is typically structured in a way that locates diagnosis, goal setting, strategic planning, and accountability in the coach rather than the client. The result can be improvement that does not outlive the engagement. This paper introduces Self-Directed Coaching (SDC) as a theory-based framework that repositions the client as the principal agent of their own developmental regulation. Grounded in self-determination theory, intentional change theory, regulatory focus theory, self-directed and self-regulated learning, cybernetic control theory, and attachment theory, SDC reframes coaching as a scaffolded process whose intended end-state is reduced dependence on formal coaching support. The framework’s central mechanism is self-regulatory internalization, the progressive transfer of coaching functions from an external agent to the client’s own regulatory repertoire. SDC is organized arou

papers.title: Post-Training on the Clock: Specializing a Small Language Model on a Consumer GPU
papers.summary: Abstract How should a language model be specialized for a target task when training is limited to one consumer GPU and a few hours? We study the allocation of a nominal three-hour training budget, with up to 0.3 additional hours, between supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). We use tool calling as a case study because of its practical relevance to language-model agents and its verifiable outputs. Using Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct with low-rank adaptation on an RTX 5060 Ti with 16 GB of memory, we compare SFT, GRPO, and six sequential SFT-to-GRPO allocations. Training uses a filtered mixture of xLAM function-calling examples and Hammer irrelevance examples, covering both call construction and abstention when no offered tool is suitable. Evaluation reports xLAM exact tool-call and function-name accuracies for local call construction, BFCL-v3 Single-turn FC (agg) for external function calling, BFCL-v3 Irrelevance (agg) for abstention, and MMLU, MATH-500, and IFEval for selected general capabilities. The suffix (agg) denotes study-specific averages of selected subset accuracies weighted by subset size. At the last evaluated checkpoints within 3.3 reported hours, SFT achieves the highest xLAM exact tool-call accuracy (82.82%), compared with 69.13% for GRPO alone. Selected hybrid allocations improve external function-calling accuracy over SFT, with dif

papers.title: KAIROS: Stateful, Context-Aware Power-Efficient Agentic Inference Serving
papers.summary: Power has become a central bottleneck for AI inference. This problem is becoming more urgent as agentic AI emerges as a major workload class, yet prior power-management techniques focus almost entirely on single-turn LLM serving. Our analysis shows that agentic serving behaves fundamentally differently: each request carries long-lived context that evolves across tool-interleaved turns, and lowering GPU frequency can push the system into a thrashing regime where memory pressure sharply worsens both performance and power efficiency. These observations show that power optimization for agentic serving requires rethinking. We present KAIROS, a context-aware power optimization system for agentic AI serving. KAIROS uses agent context as a first-class control signal to jointly manage GPU frequency, per-instance concurrency, and multi-instance request placement. This enables KAIROS to save power when memory headroom exists while avoiding thrashing and preserving performance targets. At a high level, KAIROS tracks requests at agent granularity, adapts local control to context growth and agent progress, and routes agents across instances to jointly improve power efficiency and memory stability. Evaluated across diverse software and data engineering agentic tasks, KAIROS achieves an average of 27% (up to 39.8%) power reduction while meeting the performance targets.

papers.title: An AI Literacy Checkpoint Framework for Critical Evaluation of AI-Generated Content in Higher Education
papers.summary: Abstract The rapid adoption of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in higher education has created a significant assessment gap, as students increasingly submit AI-assisted work without demonstrating competencies required to verify facts, authenticate sources, identify hallucinations, assess bias, uphold academic integrity, and critically reflect on AI use. Although several AI literacy frameworks have been proposed, including those by Fan et al. (2025), AI4K12 (Touretzky et al., 2019), and international policy reports (UNESCO, 2019, 2021, 2022), no automated and empirically validated system has existed to assess AI-assisted academic submissions systematically. This study introduces the AI Literacy Checkpoint Framework (ALCF), a six-checkpoint automated sequential pipeline that evaluates Source Verification (CP1), Fact Verification (CP2), Hallucination Detection (CP3), Bias and Fairness Assessment (CP4), Academic Integrity (CP5), and Reflection and Critical Thinking (CP6). The framework was evaluated through three progressively larger sets of constructed submissions to examine feasibility, robustness, and scalability. Phase 1 (\(\:N=10\) submissions) established proof of concept; Phase 2 (\(\:N=20\) submissions) introduced more complex error scenarios and structured reporting; and Phase 3 (\(\:N=50\) submissions) provided the primary evaluation with comparative baseline s

papers.title: MUSE: An Interactive Meta-Agent for Understanding and Steering LLM-powered Data Science Systems
papers.summary: Recent advances in large language models have enabled a new class of agentic data science systems that allow users to complete complex data science workflows through natural language. Although these systems can significantly reduce manual effort, it remains difficult to diagnose their behavior and steer the reasoning process when failures or unexpected outputs occur. We present MUSE, an interactive meta-agent that enhances user understanding and control of agentic data science systems by (1) dynamically restructuring low-level execution traces into multiple semantic levels that support navigation from high-level overviews to low-level implementation details; (2) enabling users to reference specific workflow steps in context to ask grounded questions, provide feedback, and revise problematic steps without manually locating relevant execution history; and (3) supporting mixed-initiative steering by surfacing suspicious steps for inspection, scaffolding the repair process, and translating user repair intent into contextualized instructions for the underlying agent. In a between-subjects study (n = 15), MUSE improved task efficiency and increased users’ confidence in understanding and steering agentic data science workflows.

papers.title: CFTR regulation of ROS-mediated cellular injury and immune dysregulation in cystic fibrosis
papers.summary: Cystic fibrosis (CF) is a life-limiting autosomal recessive disorder caused by biallelic loss-of-function mutations in the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) gene, most commonly F508del. Mutant CFTR disrupts transepithelial ion transport and intracellular redox homeostasis, leading to excessive accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS). Evidence from cohort studies, human airway organoid models, and single-cell transcriptomic analyses published between 2020 and 2026 has prompted substantial revision of the prevailing linear model of CF pathogenesis. These studies demonstrate that misfolded CFTR can independently initiate oxidative stress and low-grade inflammation in the absence of microbial colonization. Mitochondrial ROS (mitoROS) constitute a central signaling hub linking F508del-induced protein misfolding to transcriptional suppression of the Nrf2 antioxidant program, constitutive activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome, and dysregulation of TLR-cytokine cascades. Triple CFTR modulator regimens, including elexacaftor-tezacaftor-ivacaftor (ETI) and the once-daily combination vanzacaftor/tezacaftor/deutivacaftor (Alyftrek, FDA-approved December 2024 for patients ≥6 years carrying at least one F508del or other Alyftrek-responsive CFTR variant; pivotal SKYLINE 102/103 trials demonstrated non-inferiority versus ETI in largely ETI-eligible populations), h

papers.title: Evaluation of state-of-the-art models for improving the diagnosis of mango tree diseases through supervised learning of symptom images in Burkina Faso
papers.summary: Abstract In Burkina Faso, the mango industry faces numerous phytosanitary constraints. This situation is exacerbated by producers’ lack of knowledge about diseases and their symptoms and the low uptake of control technologies. This study aims to develop a tool using artificial intelligence-based approaches for better integrated management of the main diseases affecting mango trees. Surveys conducted in 40 mango orchards yielded 11,001 images of the characteristic symptoms of three major diseases, including 4,527 for anthracnose caused by Colletotrichum gloeosporioides , 3,038 for bacterial disease caused by Xanthomonas citri pv. mangiferaeindicae and 3,436 for dieback caused by Lasiodiplodia spp. The data underwent several preprocessing steps. To ensure a balance between disease classes, 3,000 images per class were selected, for a total of 9,000 images. The images were then annotated and used for training with the pre-trained YOLOv11 model. Following training, three models were formed : V2-3 M (MAP@50 = 50,3%; precision = 55,1%; recall = 49,1%; F1-score = 51,9%), V3-3 M (MAP@50 = 23%; precision = 56,8% ; recall = 26,7%; F1-score = 36,3%), and V4-3 M (MAP@50 = 46,8%; precision = 52%; recall = 45,3%; F1-score = 48,4%). The most effective model is the V2-3 M, as it combines 55,1% accuracy, 50,3% (MAP@50, 49,1% recall and F1-score = 51,9%). In order to improve diagnosis and phytosa

papers.title: Feedback from e-assessment and e-tasks in mathematics education – a narrative review of the literature
papers.summary: Abstract This narrative literature review examines published peer-reviewed research from 2012 to 2024 on feedback originating from e-assessment and e-tasks in the context of secondary and university mathematics teaching. The review identified 33 papers meeting the criteria set. First, we explored trends in e-feedback research over the period, showing how they reflect recent developments in digital resources and e-assessment. In this time, emphasis moved from concerns with accurate scoring to providing elaborated feedback including metacognitive support, and to studies of teacher professional development for using e-assessment. Emerging principles for the design of e-feedback relate to timing, personalization and adaptivity, interactivity and teacher support. Similarly, design principles have emerged to support student-centred approaches to teaching, and to encourage self-regulation and metacognition. Studies also investigated how teacher agency operates across diverse digital contexts—designing tasks that enable useful feedback, interpreting learning analytics, and orchestrating class activities using feedback. This set of papers reveals considerable change over the period reviewed. We envisage the diversity of research goals to continue as the capacity to provide insightful automated feedback on e-tasks to teachers and students evolves with evolving technology.

papers.title: Viewpoints on inclusive education at the end of initial teacher preparation: Q methodology research
papers.summary: Abstract This study used Q methodology to explore the perspectives on inclusive education held by 44 student teachers completing their initial teacher education (ITE) programme at Qatar University. Participants ranked 44 statements along a quasi‐normal distribution; factor analysis yielded four distinct viewpoints. The first frames inclusion as a shared professional commitment owned by every teacher within a collaborative ecosystem. The second regards mainstream inclusion as structurally unrealistic and assigns responsibility primarily to specialist staff. The third is the most affirmative orientation, grounding inclusion in rights and expressing confidence in its outcomes and systemic feasibility. The fourth combines a genuine moral commitment to inclusion with a critical view that students with special needs are being inadequately supported and that teachers lack the preparation to address this. The coexistence of these four viewpoints within a single cohort that completed the same programme suggests that the current single‐course structure has not produced a coherent or shared professional framework for inclusive teaching. The programme appears to have established a normative baseline around inclusion as a principled commitment while leaving significant gaps in conceptual clarity, professional responsibility and practical readiness. These gaps carry direct implications for I

papers.title: Digital-Twin-Driven Predictive Maintenance and Fault-Tolerant Control for Electrified Agricultural Machinery: A Multiphysics and Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for PMSM In-Wheel Drives
papers.summary: Electrified agricultural machinery increasingly relies on permanent-magnet synchronous motor drives that must remain dependable under variable traction, terrain-induced vibration, thermal cycling, contamination, and intermittent duty. Existing work offers mature methods for motor fault diagnosis, digital twins, predictive maintenance, and distributed-drive fault-tolerant control, but their health information is often not shared across diagnosis, maintenance, and control. This article develops a multiphysics digital-twin framework in which electrical, thermal, mechanical, and vibrational evidence maintains a probabilistic health belief that constrains both supervisory maintenance decisions and torque redistribution. The framework formalizes observability, uncertainty-aware health factors, deterministic safety shielding, multi-rate fallback logic, and agriculture-specific traction constraints. Reproducible low-fidelity numerical studies provide preliminary support for context-conditioned residual diagnosis and the revised thermal-continuity trade-off underlying health-aware derating, including robustness and sensitivity analyses. They do not validate sim-to-real transfer or the reinforcement-learning policy itself; those hypotheses remain open for dynamometer and hardware-in-the-loop testing. The results are therefore interpreted as mechanism-level evidence rather than field-perf

papers.title: Exploring or Exploiting Generative AI? A Dual-Path, Dual-Horizon Theory of Employee Incremental and Radical Creativity
papers.summary: Recent research has established that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is not a unitary workplace resource: exploratory and exploitative use orientations are associated with different forms of employee creativity, and their value depends on employees' capacity to integrate generated knowledge. This article therefore does not present the basic dual path as a new discovery. Instead, it develops a theoretical integration and dynamic extension that asks why the established paths operate differently, when employees should switch between them, and how short-run augmentation can evolve into either capability accumulation or capability substitution. We distinguish expansive and consolidative modes of knowledge integration, theorize phase-congruent switching rather than static ``high-high'' ambidexterity, and position metacognition as a control mechanism that governs both immediate knowledge conversion and longer-run cognitive development. We further specify cultural tightness and psychological safety as directional boundary conditions and distinguish individual creative gains from collective idea-space diversity. The framework converts emerging empirical regularities into falsifiable propositions about task phase, context, and time, providing a research agenda for sustainable human--AI creativity.

papers.title: From Coding to Creativity: Integrating Design Thinking into IT and Technology Education
papers.summary: This study examines how the integration of Design Thinking into Information Technology (IT) and technology education can bridge technical programming skills and creative, human-centered problem-solving. Specifically, it explores how the five stages of Design Thinking empathizing, defining, ideating, prototyping, and testing shape students’ creative thinking, active engagement, and collaborative learning experiences. A qualitative research approach was employed, involving teachers, students, and school principals as key informants. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, classroom observations, and documentation of learning activities, then analyzed thematically to identify recurring patterns in teaching practices and student experiences. The findings indicate that Design Thinking creates opportunities for students to move beyond coding procedures toward developing digital solutions that respond to real users’ needs. Through collaborative ideation, iterative prototyping, and feedback-based testing, students demonstrate greater involvement in learning, explore alternative solutions, and communicate their ideas more actively. The approach also provides opportunities to develop empathy, creativity, collaboration, and a willingness to experiment with and revise initial designs. Meanwhile, teachers assume a facilitative role by guiding inquiry, supporting experimentation, an

papers.title: COVID-19: An updated comprehensive review
papers.summary: More than six years after the emergence of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) remains a complex global health challenge shaped by continued viral evolution, heterogeneous population immunity, and unequal access to prevention and care. The transition from the acute pandemic phase has changed the relationship between infection, hospitalization, and mortality, while reduced testing and surveillance complicate assessment of the contemporary burden. Ongoing diversification of Omicron descendants, waning protection against infection, and recurrent exposure have introduced additional uncertainties regarding transmissibility, immune escape, and clinical risk. Beyond acute respiratory illness, COVID-19 encompasses multisystem complications and persistent postinfectious symptoms, requiring an integrated appraisal of virological, immunological, clinical, and public health evidence. The aim of this narrative review is to critically synthesize current knowledge of SARS-CoV-2 epidemiology, genomic evolution, transmission, pathogenesis, host immune responses, and the spectrum of clinical manifestations. It also examines advances and limitations in diagnostic testing, severity-stratified therapeutics, vaccination, nonpharmaceutical interventions, and the recognition and management of long COVID. Particular attention is given to evi

papers.title: From the Rock Floor to the Cloud: A Systematic Review of State-of-the-Art NLP in Battery Life Cycle
papers.summary: This work presents a systematic review of the application of natural language processing (NLP) along the entire battery life cycle, instead of reviewing one stage or method, and introduces a novel conceptual technical language processing (TLP) framework for the European Union (EU)’s proposed digital battery passport (DBP) and other general battery predictions, as the main objective. It follows the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) method and employs three reputable databases or search engines, including Google Scholar, Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers Xplore (IEEE Xplore), and Scopus, searched in October, 2025. The search criteria are ’text’, ’language processing’, and ’battery’, while the exclusion criteria are non-relevant papers and those published before 2017, which were applied to all databases, except IEEE Xplore because it turned up fewer results. Consequently, it assesses 274 scientific papers before the critical review of the final 66 relevant papers. We publicly provide artifacts of the review for validation and possible reproducibility. The findings show that new NLP tasks are emerging in the battery domain, which facilitate materials discovery and other stages of the life cycle. Notwithstanding, challenges remain, such as the lack of standard benchmarks. The proposed TLP framework, which incorporates agentic

papers.title: TARMAC as a taxonomy for robot manipulation in chemistry
papers.summary: Abstract Laboratory automation has benefited substantially from well-defined protocols and machine-readable representations of chemical procedures. Yet a long tail of context-dependent physical tasks, including setup, adjustment, and cleanup, continues to require manual intervention or bespoke robotic implementations tailored to individual workflows and platforms. This study examines whether this apparent diversity can be organized into a structured and reusable action space. TARMAC ( TA xonomy for R obot MA nipulation in C hemistry), an empirical taxonomy of laboratory actions, is derived through a bottom-up analysis of instructional chemistry practice. The taxonomy comprises 18 physically meaningful primitives organized by three dimensions: wrench dependence, actuation directness, and motion periodicity. Evaluation through cross-corpus protocol decomposition and robotic instantiation addresses expressive coverage and proof-of-concept executability. Across 23 procedures, 904 of 917 manipulative steps map to the primitive set, while robotic tests instantiate 8 primitives in five tasks across four robotic configurations. Together, these results indicate that laboratory manipulation can be organized as a structured action space across the examined contexts. TARMAC therefore provides a descriptive basis for organizing and comparing manipulation requirements across experimental wor

papers.title: Physics-informed Bayesian optimization for quantitative high-resolution transmission electron microscopy
papers.summary: Abstract Quantitative high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) provides an indispensable means to understand structure-property relationships in atomic dimensions. Successful quantification requires reliable retrieval of essential atomic structural information despite artifacts arising from practically unavoidable imaging imperfections. Experimental observation combined with model-based iterative image simulation has enabled broad applications in quantitative structural and chemical determination of objects spanning zero to three dimensions. However, the large number of parameters involved makes the current multi-step, user-supervised iterative approach highly time-consuming, restricting its use to small sample areas and experienced users. In this work, we implement and apply a physics-informed Bayesian optimization (BO) framework to advance HRTEM quantification toward full automation and large-field-of-view analysis. Unlike conventional optimization methods, our approach adopts a stepwise strategy that fully leverages BO’s strength in handling high-dimensional parameter spaces, while its probabilistic engine efficiently refines the parameter space for rapid quantification. Using a BaTiO 3 single crystal that contains heavy, medium, and light elements as a model system, we demonstrate that the three-dimensional crystal structure can be determined from a single H

papers.title: A closed-loop framework for perovskite precursor additive discovery
papers.summary: Efficient discovery of precursor additives is essential for improving the performance of perovskite solar cells, yet the large chemical space makes conventional trial-and-error screening inefficient. Here we show that LEAP (LLM-driven Exploration via Active Learning for Perovskites), a closed-loop framework combining a domain-specialized language model with active learning, prioritizes perovskite precursor additives under low-data conditions. The model extracts mechanism-relevant knowledge from the literature and converts it into interpretable molecular descriptors for uncertainty-aware Bayesian optimization. On an evaluation drawn from unseen literature, the specialized model provides more mechanism-consistent answers than the tested general-purpose models. In an expert-guided proof-of-concept study, two later-round additives increase average device power conversion efficiencies to 20.13% and 20.87%, compared with 19.25% for the control, and the best device reaches 21.32%. Because only a limited number of candidates are tested prospectively, these results provide preliminary evidence that literature-grounded molecular representations, Bayesian optimization, and expert assessment can support additive discovery for perovskite solar cells. Discovering effective perovskite precursor additives is challenging due to the vast chemical space. Here, the authors present a closed-loop ac

papers.title: Teacher Creativity and Innovative Classroom Practices in Secondary Schools
papers.summary: Teacher creativity has become increasingly consequential as secondary schools respond to heterogeneous learners, digital transformation, generative artificial intelligence, and demands for higher-order thinking. This study addresses a specific research gap: existing scholarship frequently measures teachers’ creativity, digital competence, or innovative behavior separately, but rarely examines how creative capacity is translated into observable and sustainable classroom innovation. The proposed study conceptualizes this translation as a Creativity-to-Practice Translation Framework, integrating creative self-efficacy, pedagogical adaptability, digital/AI agency, collaborative school climate, and instructional experimentation.Particular attention is given to whether teachers who perceive themselves as creative actually implement differentiated tasks, inquiry-oriented activities, multimodal resources, AI-assisted lesson design, collaborative problem solving, and formative experimentation in secondary classrooms.

papers.title: Reimagining adolescent education with ephegogy: generative AI and active learning in practice
papers.summary: Purpose This paper introduces ephegogy, a theory addressing the gap between traditional educational models and adolescents' developmental needs in artificial intelligence (AI)-augmented societies. Blending constructivism, connectivism and generativism, it explores how integrating generative AI (GenAI) and active learning can scaffold motivation, autonomy, and relevance for adolescent learners. Design/methodology/approach A mixed-methods case study conducted in a single secondary-school geography course during 2024–2025. Quantitative data came from matched pre- and post-intervention surveys measuring motivation and self-efficacy (N = 17; N = 11 for the self-efficacy composite) and locus of control (N = 12), using instruments adapted for an under-14, predominantly English-as-an-additional-language cohort. A separate matched engagement survey (N = 24) and an end-of-course co-creation survey (N = 33) provided further data. Qualitative data comprised 74 individual student reflections analysed thematically using the cultural-historical activity theory (CHAT) framework, alongside open-text survey responses from 74 students. The study was designed using three frameworks (self-determination theory, ephegogy and CHAT). Findings Findings are associational and exploratory, specific to this pilot. Composite motivation increased significantly (p = 0.043, d = 0.53), led by a significant rise

papers.title: Generation of synthetic clinical text: a systematic review
papers.summary: Generating medical synthetic text represents an effective solution for clinical NLP issues like sparsity and privacy. This paper conducts a systematic review on synthetic clinical text generation by formulating quantitative analysis to three research questions concerning the generation’s purpose, generation techniques, and the evaluation methods. We searched four databases including PubMed, Scopus, ScienceDirect and Web of Science for publications associated with the topic and identified 87 relevant articles out of 1148. Results showed that the generation purposes were dedicated to Trustworthy, Medical Assistance, and Language Resource themes. Prompting LLMs was the main source of synthetic text (40 articles). GPTs were the main predominant technique used to generate the text (63 articles), especially ChatGPT (47 articles). Additionally, there were four main aspects of evaluation, including similarity, privacy, structure, and utility, where utility was the prevailing method for assessment (52 articles). The synthetic medical text empowered data augmentation and clinical documentation. Using text alteration, controlling real text portions, and federated learning, generative models can produce privacy-preserving medical text. This accelerates the development of new digital health applications.

papers.title: FabDreamer: Exploring the Image-to-Physical Workflow Through AI-Assisted Layered Fabrication
papers.summary: Generative AI lets anyone create rich visual content in seconds, yet translating that content into a physically fabricable artifact still demands manual decomposition, occlusion repair, and structural verification that most tools leave entirely to the user. We present FabDreamer, an image-to-physical system that carries an image to fabrication-ready SVGs through three stages with deliberately staged AI initiative: (1) AI leads decomposition into depth-ordered layers, (2) assists on demand during creative editing with real-time 3D preview, and (3) advises on structural integrity before export. We instantiate this workflow for layered laser-cut art and evaluate it through three rounds including a formative analysis, an early prototype user evaluation (N=13), and a cross-domain practitioner study with specialists from 6 fabrication domains (N=6). Our findings show that physical awareness during design opens creative opportunities beyond error prevention, that practitioners appropriate the system’s generic geometric operations for their own domains, and that the fabrication agent covers geometry-readable constraints while domain knowledge remains with the maker.

papers.title: InsightToast: Proactive Information Retrieval & Glanceable Visualization in the Side Channel of Data-Rich Meetings
papers.summary: Missing institutional context during meetings can impede effective participation. Retrieving relevant information, often scattered across heterogeneous internal and external sources, requires costly task-switching that disrupts both individual focus and collective conversational flow, particularly detrimental during cognitively demanding tasks such as decision-making. We introduce InsightToast, a mixed-initiative application that monitors verbal discourse in real time, identifies topics and informational needs as they emerge, and proactively retrieves relevant information through a multi-agent large language model (LLM)-based pipeline integrating retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to produce source-grounded insights as succinct text and glanceable interactive charts, delivered through a peripheral interface as ephemeral toasts in the conversation’s side channel. To demonstrate the potential for yielding serendipitous insights, we showcase a usage scenario involving a knowledge base of legislative documents as the meeting’s context. We then report on a comparative study (N = 16), in which participants arrived at informed policy decisions while maintaining natural conversation flow.

papers.title: From AI literacy to brand advocacy: The roles of self-determined motivation and UTAUT factors in AI-powered online brand consultation
papers.summary: AI-powered brand consultation is becoming an important digital touchpoint, yet limited research explains how consumers’ AI capabilities translate into brand-supportive recommendation responses. This study examines how AI literacy shapes willingness to recommend AI-powered online brand consultation through technology-related beliefs and self-determined motivation in Vietnam’s digital commerce context. Drawing on an integrated AI Literacy–UTAUT–Self-Determination Theory framework, AI literacy is conceptualized as a formative higher-order capability comprising awareness, usage, evaluation, and ethics. Based on survey data from 536 Vietnamese online consumers, the proposed model was tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling. The findings show that AI literacy significantly associated with performance expectancy, effort expectancy, social influence, and facilitating conditions, with AI evaluation emerging as the most influential literacy component. Autonomy, competence, and relatedness are positively associated with motivation, while behavioral intention is significantly associated with performance expectancy, facilitating conditions, and motivation, but not by effort expectancy or social influence. papers.title: Video and digital games: Historical controversies, benefits, and risks for children and adolescents
papers.summary: Video and digital games have been the focus of sustained public and scientific debate since their commercial emergence in the late 1970s, particularly regarding their effects on children and adolescents. Early public and scientific discourse frequently portrayed gaming as a source of physical injury, addiction, aggression, social isolation, academic problems, and moral decline. However, subsequent empirical research has produced a substantially more differentiated picture of both the benefits and risks of gaming. This review examines the historical foundations of controversies surrounding video and digital games and synthesizes contemporary evidence concerning their cognitive, emotional, social, therapeutic, and physical effects. . Research indicates that moderate, purposeful gaming may improve visuospatial abilities, attentional control, problem-solving, mood regulation, social connection, and selected educational outcomes. Gaming-based interventions have also demonstrated therapeutic potential, particularly for depressive symptoms and attention-related difficulties among young people. At the same time, important risks remain, especially when gaming becomes excessive, compulsive, or disruptive to everyday functioning. papers.title: Designing a Curriculum Model Based on Artificial Intelligence and Purposeful Physical Activity to Enhance Learning Self-Regulation, Mental Health, and Psychological Well-Being among Students
papers.summary: Objective: The objective of this study was to design and validate a curriculum model based on artificial intelligence and purposeful physical activity with emphasis on enhancing learning self-regulation, mental health, and psychological well-being among students. Methods and Materials: This applied developmental study was conducted using an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design. In the qualitative phase, 20 experts in curriculum studies, educational technology, artificial intelligence in education, physical education, educational psychology, and student mental health were selected through purposive criterion-based sampling from Tehran and participated in semi-structured interviews. The interview data were analyzed using thematic analysis to extract the main dimensions, components, and indicators of the proposed curriculum model. In the quantitative phase, 384 secondary school students from Tehran were selected through multistage cluster sampling during the 2025–2026 academic year. Data were collected using a researcher-made curriculum model validation questionnaire, a learning self-regulation questionnaire, the General Health Questionnaire, and a psychological well-being scale. papers.title: Assessing the feasibility of a video-based conversational chatbot survey for measuring perceived cycling safety: A pilot study in New York City
papers.summary: Bicycle safety is essential for bikeability and transport efficiency, yet conventional surveys often fail to capture how people perceive cycling environments in real time because they depend on retrospective recall. This study proposes a video-based conversational AI chatbot survey, powered by large language models (LLMs), to collect perceptions of cycling safety and the reasons behind them. The chatbot was developed using a modular LLM architecture that integrates prompt engineering, state management, and rule-based control. Its feasibility was evaluated through a pilot study involving 16 participants across nine street segments in New York City. The method feasibility was assessed using a seven-point scale rating for user experience (i.e., ease of use, supportiveness, efficiency) and a five-point scale for chatbot usability (i.e., personality, roboticness, friendliness), yielding positive results with mean scores of 5.00 out of 7 (standard deviation = 1.60) and 3.47 out of 5 (standard deviation = 0.43), respectively.
